priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock. The case for interest is real: the reverse DCF implies just a 7.0% five-year free-cash-flow CAGR (5.05% at ten years, horizon spread 1.95pp, both well inside a range where the horizon convention is not doing the work), which sits at or below the 6.7312% three-year revenue CAGR already delivered, while Q2 2026 revenue grew 20.2% YoY and backlog grew 19.6% YoY to a record $3.16 billion, on a net-cash balance sheet with Piotroski 8 of 9 (STRONG) and a clean Beneish M-score. The company sits on the single highest-criticality bottleneck in this twelve-link chain. Against that: capture at this link is the chain's own named trap example (score 40, investability PARTIAL), meaning volume growth may not convert into equity value the way it would for a moated supplier, since MYR Group earns a bid-competed contractor margin (4.562% FY2025 operating margin) rather than an equipment or technology margin. The company's own multi-year earnings record is genuinely volatile at a scale that matters: FY2024 net income collapsed to $30.3 million from $91.0 million in FY2023 on essentially flat revenue, the signature of percentage-of-completion cost-estimate risk, and today's high cash conversion (OCF at 2.7578x net income) is flagged as probable working-capital timing rather than a durable feature. Most importantly, roughly 90% of the stock's two-year price return is price-to-sales re-rating rather than delivered per-share revenue growth (0.6504x to 1.2494x against 7.9% revenue-per-share growth), and even the 41.3% drawdown from the 2026-06-29 peak has not brought the multiple back to its 2023 level. Crowdedness is left unresolved rather than picked flatteringly: PCS Axis A reads DARK at 73.5 under an ADVISORY gate with unreadable control fixtures, Axis B reads SATURATED on only 5 analysts with an unusable institutional-ownership field above 100%, and the chain-level UNDISCOVERED judgment (crowdedness 30) is an analytical call about the corner, not a clean measurement of this issuer, a tension the price action itself argues against (something clearly found and then sold this name hard, which is not the behavior of a name nobody has noticed). Net: a cheap forward bar sitting on top of an already-large, only-partly-unwound re-rating, at a link whose economics genuinely cap how much of the volume upside reaches equity holders. That combination earns WATCH with five specific, dated triggers rather than an entry zone I could defend if the current price level turns out to still be inside the unwind.
bull: Cheapest forward bar in the campaign's complete O1 or O2 batch measured against delivered growth: the reverse DCF implies just a 7.0% five-year free-cash-flow CAGR (5.05% at ten years), at or below the 6.7312% three-year revenue CAGR already achieved, while Q2 2026 revenue grew 20.2% YoY and backlog grew 19.6% YoY to a record $3.16 billion, an acceleration the implied bar does not require to continue.

Balance sheet imposes no constraint on riding the buildout: net debt to EBITDA of -0.5705x (net cash), Piotroski 8 of 9 (STRONG, 9 of 9 inputs present), and a clean Beneish M-score of -2.206 against a -1.78 review threshold (12 of 12 inputs present).

Sits on the single highest-criticality bottleneck in the whole twelve-link chain, grid-interconnect, bottleneck criticality HIGH and named as the chain's slowest step, with double-sided exposure: the T&D segment builds the interconnection itself and the C&I segment names data centers among the facility types it wires, plus two acquisitions (Valley Electric and Comet Electric, closed 2026-07-01) that management says enhance the C&I side specifically.
bear: Capture is the chain's own named trap example at this exact link (score 40, investability PARTIAL): MYR Group earns a bid-competed contractor margin, 4.562% GAAP operating margin for FY2025, not an equipment or technology margin, so a larger AI-driven volume wave is not guaranteed to reach equity holders the way it would for a moated supplier.

Earnings and margins are demonstrably volatile at a scale that matters: FY2024 net income collapsed to $30.3 million from $91.0 million in FY2023 on essentially flat revenue ($3,362.3 million against $3,643.9 million), the signature of percentage-of-completion cost-estimate revisions on fixed-price contracts, the same mechanism now running favorably in FY2025 and H1 2026 ('significant changes in our estimated gross profit on certain projects... favorable job close outs'). Today's earnings-quality read rests on one strong recovery sitting on top of that demonstrated history.

About 90% of the stock's two-year price return is price-to-sales re-rating rather than delivered growth: price rose 107.2% (142.07 to 294.42) from 2023-08-31 to 2026-08-28 while revenue per share rose only 7.9% ($218.42 to $235.63), and price-to-sales roughly tripled in between (0.6504x to a peak near 1.9x to 2.1x in June 2026) before settling at 1.2494x today, still about 1.9x its 2023 level even after a 41.3% drawdown from the 501.13 peak.

rows.market_implied_note: Approximate, reasoned rather than solved: since the 7.0% FCF CAGR barely exceeds the 6.7312% achieved revenue CAGR, the price appears to assume little to no operating-margin expansion beyond the FY2025 level of 4.562%.
rows.structural_reason: H1 2026 consolidated operating margin (6.37%) already exceeds every full fiscal year in the 2018-2025 record (prior high 4.75% in FY2021), and it shows up in both segments (T&D 9.6%, C&I 8.3% operating margin in H1 2026 per the 8-K segment table), not one segment's favorable close-outs alone, which is at least consistent with a mix shift toward higher-value work rather than a single-project fluke.
rows.leading_indicator: Quarterly consolidated operating margin sustaining at or above 6% through Q4 2026, rather than reverting toward the FY2018-2024 average of roughly 3.5% once the currently favorable job close-outs (management's own stated driver) roll off. This is watch_triggers[1] on this file.
rows.why: Margin history is volatile and this is a genuinely aggressive assumption relative to it, which is why the structural reason and leading indicator above are both named rather than assumed.

rows.market_implied_note: The solve as filed does not decompose a reinvestment return separately from the headline FCF CAGR. Recorded as a data gap in this row rather than invented.
rows.why: The company's own disclosed non-GAAP Return on Invested Capital ran 26.7% LTM against 12.7% a year earlier, a real, filed figure, well above the reverse DCF's 9% discount rate. Base rate (roughly 40-50% of top-quartile ROIC firms stay there after ten years) argues for meaningful decay rather than persistence at 26.7%, so 15% mid-path is a decay case, not an extrapolation of the peak.
rows.leading_indicator: LTM ROIC as disclosed each quarter; a slide back toward the low-to-mid teens over the next two to three quarters would confirm decay, a hold near 25% plus would say the current level is more durable than the base rate implies.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so matters. The solve's 2.5% perpetual growth sits at or below the long-run nominal GDP ceiling this repo's own base rates cite, and is the one input this dive would not change for a bid-competed contractor with no visible moat.

rows.note: The forward-implied bar (7.0% five-year FCF CAGR) is cheap against delivered growth (6.7312% achieved, 20.2% YoY last quarter), which argues for a positive gap. Two things cap it from becoming a clean bullish call: capture at this link is the chain's own trap example (score 40), so volume growth may not convert to equity value at the rate the growth numbers alone would suggest; and about 90% of the stock's two-year price return is already price-to-sales re-rating rather than delivered growth, a re-rating only 41% unwound from its June 2026 peak. Net: modestly positive on the forward numbers, substantially offset by a capture ceiling and a multiple that has not fully round-tripped.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market is treating MYR Group's 41.3% drawdown from its 2026-06-29 peak as a correction of a story that ran too far, when the forward-implied growth bar left behind by that drawdown (7.0% five-year FCF CAGR) is now cheap relative to what the company is currently delivering (record backlog up 19.6% YoY, revenue up 20.2% YoY), even though the underlying multiple has not returned to its pre-story 2023 level.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: This looks like a thin-coverage momentum unwind rather than a fundamentals-driven repricing: with only 5 sell-side analysts and no dedicated data-center or grid-capex segment disclosure to anchor a bottom-up model, a name that ran nearly 3x in nine months on a narrative is more exposed to indiscriminate, valuation-agnostic selling once sentiment turns than a well-covered name would be, and the decline beginning before, not after, a genuinely strong earnings print is consistent with that category of error rather than with a fundamentals-driven reappraisal.
independence_test.falsification: By the Q3 2026 earnings release (expected late October or early November 2026): if backlog growth decelerates back toward MYR Group's own trailing multi-year average pace (high single digits YoY) rather than sustaining the high-teens growth seen in Q2 2026, AND consolidated operating margin falls back under 6.0%, the 'thin-coverage overreaction' reading is wrong and the drawdown correctly anticipated a genuine slowdown in the business, not just in the stock.

earnings_quality.basis: Grade B: a clean mechanical core carrying two mild, disclosed and defensible flags, not a clean A and not a Beneish-breach C. Clean: Beneish M-score of -2.206 against the -1.78 review threshold (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found); Piotroski 8 of 9 (STRONG, 9 of 9 inputs found), the sole miss being a modest current-ratio decline (1.400 FY2024 to 1.334 FY2025) consistent with funding backlog growth through working capital rather than a liquidity problem; Altman Z of 5.97 (SAFE); DSO improved to 60.25 days in FY2025 from a 70.90-day spike in FY2024, no sustained upward drift; capex-to-depreciation stable in a 1.17x to 1.43x band across FY2022-2025, unremarkable for a growing fleet-and-equipment contractor; no auditor change or CFO turnover found (Kelly Huntington has held the CFO role since February 2023 per web search, not exhaustive), no related-party dealings found in the fetched document. Flags: (1) accruals of -13.29% of average assets in FY2025 (net income $118.416M against operating cash flow $326.567M, average total assets $1,566.4415M) exceed even the 10% review-band magnitude the analyst-sources base rates flag for accrual quality, and the swing has been widening (FY2023 +1.34%, FY2024 -3.71%, FY2025 -13.29%); the direction is conservative, cash exceeds earnings rather than the aggressive earnings-inflating direction the accrual-anomaly literature actually warns about, but the magnitude and the trend are large enough to name rather than wave through, and the profile's own risk note calls this level of cash conversion probable working-capital timing rather than durable conversion for a percentage-of-completion contractor; (2) the company's own multi-year earnings record is genuinely volatile at a scale that matters for a $4.6B issuer: FY2024 operating income of $54.082M was less than half FY2023's $129.093M on essentially flat revenue, which the industry's percentage-of-completion accounting attributes to unfavorable cost-estimate revisions on fixed-price contracts, the same mechanism now running favorably in FY2025 and H1 2026 per management's own language ('favorable job close outs'). Not A because of (1) and (2); not C because neither is a Beneish breach, a sustained DSO or deferred-revenue drift, or an undisclosed one-time claim, everything above is on the face of the filing or the companyfacts series. The grade does not cap this dive's verdict: WATCH is reached on the expectations-gap and crowdedness analysis, not on the earnings-quality veto.
